Purpose To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing the diagnostic performance in fracture detection between AI and clinicians in peer-reviewed publications and the gray literature (ie, articles published on preprint repositories).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Artificial Intelligence in Fracture Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】Meta-analysis with a hierarchical model to calculate pooled sensitivity and specificity was used.

【Abstract · abstract-1-9】For internal validation test sets, the pooled sensitivity was 92% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 91% (95% CI: 85, 95) for clinicians, and the pooled specificity was 91% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 92% (95% CI: 89, 92) for clinicians.

evidence.text: Meta-analysis with a hierarchical model to calculate pooled sensitivity and specificity was used.

For internal validation test sets, the pooled sensitivity was 92% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 91% (95% CI: 85, 95) for clinicians, and the pooled specificity was 91% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 92% (95% CI: 89, 92) for clinicians.
